_README: OUR editorial judgments — NOT client data. menu.json is the client's source of truth.
clean_menu.py reads this at build time. Edit here and re-run; never hand-edit menu_clean.json.
Everything in this file is a decision we made and can defend, not a fact from the client.
_meal_times_note: Which meals each category suits. Serving-time judgment, NOT a health or nutrition claim.
Low stakes: a kebab tagged dinner-only when someone wants it at lunch harms nobody.
Store opens 06:00, so 'breakfast' is a real window even though there is no breakfast menu.
_step_types_note: All 204 customisation steps are labelled 'Please Select' / 'Choose 1' in the client data,
so a step cannot be told from its own label. We infer the step's purpose from its OPTION
titles instead — there are only 16 distinct ones across all 735 option rows.
Matching is exact (case-insensitive) on option titles; unmatched steps fall back to
default_step_label. This maps STRUCTURE, not nutrition — which is why it is safe where
default_step_label: Please choose one of the following
_display_fixes_note: Typo fixes for DISPLAY TEXT ONLY. The original item_step_option_id is always preserved in
the output — that ID is what the cart backend expects, typo or not. Keys are matched
case-insensitively against the raw option title.
_excluded_items_note: Items withheld from the AI's menu, by item_id. Both are priced 0.00 and we cannot ask the
client whether that is intentional. A bot that adds a free item to a cart looks broken, so
we hide them rather than guess. 'Burger King' is also the only variation item in the file
(one variation priced 11), which suggests its 0 base price is a data error.
